http://www.bgnes.com/politics/moldovan-p.text: Moldova’s parliament has approved a new government led by Prime Minister Vasile Tofan after he presented his cabinet’s programme, pledging to revive the economy and keep the country on its European path, TVP World reported. Moldova, one of Europe’s poorest countries and one facing uncertainty stemming from the war in neighbouring Ukraine, recorded economic growth of 2.4% last year. Growth of around 2% is forecast for this year. “Our programme is called The European Economy, the Efficient State. That is the commitment we will work toward, and that is how we want to be judged,” the 45-year-old financier Tofan told lawmakers. President Maia Sandu’s Party of Action and Solidarity (PAS) holds a majority in the 101-seat parliament, and Tofan’s nomination was backed by 53 lawmakers from the ruling party. The opposition abstained from the vote. Tofan said his government aims to sign Moldova’s accession agreement with the European Union by the end of 2028 and prepare the country for EU membership by 2030. To achieve this, the cabinet intends to open all EU negotiating chapters by the end of this year. Moldova, together with Ukraine, was granted EU candidate status and has so far opened two of the six negotiation clusters. Tofan takes office following the surprise resignation of his predecessor, Alexandru Munteanu, who served as prime minister for only eight months. The new prime minister also pledged to reduce the country’s budget deficit by two percentage points by 2029. It currently stands at 20 billion Moldovan lei (about $1.1 billion). He said tax reform, cutting administrative burdens and improving businesses’ access to financing would be essential. Among the cabinet’s priorities are the privatisation of at least 10 state-owned enterprises, encouraging investment in technology and artificial intelligence, increasing exports of high value-added products, and reducing the size of the shadow economy. Located between Ukraine and EU member state Romania, Moldova has a Romanian-speaking majority and a sizeable Russian-speaking minority. For decades, political power in the country has alternated between parties advocating closer integration with Europe and those favouring stronger ties with Moscow. | BGNES

Photograph: Hilary Wardhaugh/Getty Images Vanuatu One dead and more than 30 missing after ferry sinks off Vanuatu coast in rough seas Prime minister’s office tells families of those missing ‘the nation stands with you’ as search and rescue efforts continue Guardian staff and agencies Sat 12 Sep 2026 22.39 EDT Last modified on Sat 12 Sep 2026 22.42 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google One person has died and more than 30 are missing after a ferry sank off the coast of Vanuatu , the country’s government says. The vessel, MV Matui, had set sail with more than 40 passengers and crew on Friday from the island of Santo to Ambae island in very rough seas, but did not arrive. “Our hearts and prayers are with the families who have lost loved ones,” Vanuatu prime minister Jotham Napat’s office said in a statement on Sunday. “Search and rescue operations are continuing.” Fifteen of those onboard have been “accounted for alive” and one body has been recovered, the statement said. “Over 30 people remain missing at sea,” it said. “To the survivors, we ⁠pray for your strength and recovery. To the families of ​those ​missing and those we ​have lost, please know that the nation stands ​with you ‌in this time ​of ​grief.” An investigation into potential negligence has been launched. “This loss appears to be the result of strong winds and marine warnings not being heeded, and possibly of negligence including overloading of the vessel,” the statement added. The Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre in New Caledonia said it was assisting with the search, and a French Armed Forces aircraft was deployed on Sunday morning. The centre said 12 people were located on Sunday morning. Matai Seremaiah, the member of parliament for Luganville who is assisting in the search, said efforts would concentrate on the south-east coast where currents may have carried survivors.
